labels.text: How can I help you today?

S17.01.note: The heading "AGI said:" is screen-reader only (sp-visually-hidden), so sighted users see no name; the model name appears only after the answer finishes.
steps: Type any question in the box that says "How can I help you today?" and send it.
Wait until the answer stops typing.
Compare the answer with your question: the answer is in its own bubble styled differently from your message.
Look at the small line under the answer after it finishes: it shows the model name and the time taken.
S17.01.where: Side panel: type in the box that says "How can I help you today?", press send, then look at the answer

steps: Type a question that asks for a list with bold text, for example a short guide, in the box that says "How can I help you today?".
Send it and watch the answer while it is still arriving.
Check that text keeps appearing piece by piece before the answer ends.
When it ends, check that bold text, lists and code blocks are shown formatted, not as raw symbols.
S17.02.where: Side panel: send a question that gets a long answer with formatting

S17.03.note: The line sits in a role=status, aria-live=polite region, so it is announced. The mark is an image, not an animated spinner, as far as the code shows.
steps: Type a question in the box that says "How can I help you today?" and send it.
Right after sending, look below your message for a small AGI mark with the word "Preparing".
Check that the "Preparing" line disappears once the answer text starts to appear.
Optionally, wait for the "Reading the page" wording on page-based requests (not verified how often it shows).
S17.03.where: Side panel: send a message and look under your message before the first words arrive

S17.04.needs: a request that makes the assistant use tools, such as a web search
S17.04.note: The disclosure shows steps and time, not the model's reasoning text; the "Extended thinking" toggle in the composer is a separate setting.
steps: Send a request that needs a tool, for example a web search about today's news.
While it works, look above the answer for a line starting with "Working for" plus the elapsed time.
Click that line to expand it.
When it finishes, check the expanded section lists the steps the assistant took, with the time and step count.
S17.04.where: Side panel: send a request that makes the assistant use tools (for example a web search), then click the collapsed line above the answer that starts with "Working for" or "Worked for"

S17.05.needs: a request that makes the assistant use tools, such as a web search
S17.05.note: The row text is the step's own summary, not the raw tool name; the tool name only sets the row icon, as far as the code shows.
steps: Send a request that uses a tool, such as a web search.
Expand the line above the answer that starts with "Working for" or "Worked for".
Click a step row to open it.
Check the row shows what the step was, its status (for example failed or cancelled), and under it the "Request" and "Result" sections.
S17.05.where: Side panel: after a request that used tools, expand the "Worked for" line above the answer, then click a step row

S17.06.needs: a question that makes the assistant use web sources
S17.06.note: Chips appear only when the model returns citations; whether a given answer has them depends on the model.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web information, for example a news question.
When the answer finishes, look for small link chips with a site name (for example a domain) inside the answer text.
Hover or focus one chip to see its source card.
Check that the chip opens the source page in a new tab when clicked.
S17.06.where: Side panel: ask a question that needs web sources, then look for small site-name chips inside the answer text

S17.07.needs: a question that makes the assistant use web sources
S17.07.note: The list is shown only after the answer finishes, not while it streams.
steps: Send a question that uses web sources and wait for the answer to finish.
Look under the answer for a line with a globe icon and the text "N sources".
Click that line to expand the list.
Check the list shows each source with its title, and that clicking one opens it in a new tab.
S17.07.where: Side panel: under a finished answer that used sources, click the "N sources" line to open the list

S17.08.needs: a request that makes the assistant produce a file
S17.08.note: The open and download buttons are icon-only; their words show as tooltips and screen-reader labels.
steps: Send a request that asks the assistant to create a downloadable file.
When the answer finishes, look under it for a file card showing the file name and a type label (for example PDF) or the word File.
Hover the open button to see the tooltip "Open <file name>"; click it.
Hover and click the download button, labelled "Download <file name>", and check the file saves.
S17.08.where: Side panel: ask the assistant to make a file (for example a text or spreadsheet file); the file card appears under the answer

S17.09.needs: a request that makes the assistant create an artifact
S17.09.note: The card code is in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts, not generatedFiles.ts as the plan's code line says.
steps: Send a request that asks for an artifact, for example a small web page or code file.
When the answer finishes, look under it for a card showing the artifact title and a line that starts with "Artifact".
Click the "Open" button on the card.
Check the artifact panel opens beside the chat and the button now reads "Hide"; click "Hide" to close it.
S17.09.where: Side panel: ask for an artifact (for example a small web page); the artifact card appears under the answer, then click "Open"

S17.10.needs: a request that makes the assistant produce an image
S17.10.note: If the image cannot be shown, the text is "<file name> could not be shown here. Open it instead."
steps: Send a request that asks for a picture, for example a simple drawing.
Wait for the text "Loading image…" to turn into the picture.
Click the picture to open it in the viewer.
Hover the download button, labelled "Download <file name>", and click it to save the image.
S17.10.where: Side panel: ask the assistant to make an image; the image appears in the answer

labels.text: This card is read-only in Chrome.

S17.13.needs: a request that makes the assistant return a card
S17.13.note: Which requests produce cards was not traced; the card code is in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts.
steps: Send a request that returns a card, for example places near a location.
Look under the answer for a card with a headline, text and a list or buttons.
Click a card button and check it opens the link in a new tab.
In a card that cannot take input in Chrome, check the text "This card is read-only in Chrome." appears.
S17.13.where: Side panel: ask a question that the assistant answers with a card (for example places on a map); the card appears under the answer

S17.15.note: The button copies the raw answer text (msg.content), so markdown symbols such as ** or # may appear in the paste; on failure it shows "Could not copy. Try again."
steps: Wait for an answer to finish.
Hover the copy icon under the answer to see the tooltip "Copy response".
Click it, then paste into a text field elsewhere.
Check the whole answer text is pasted.
S17.15.where: Side panel: under a finished answer, click the copy icon button labelled "Copy response"

S17.19.needs: none for the basic button; a signed-in account for the model menu
S17.19.note: The button appears only on the most recent answer, and not while streaming or on an error or cancelled answer.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the icon under the answer to see the tooltip "Try again".
Click it.
Check the answer is replaced by a new attempt for the same question, and that the old answer is gone.
S17.19.where: Side panel: on the latest answer, click the icon button labelled "Try again" under it

S17.20.needs: a way to make an answer fail (for example turn off the internet before sending)
S17.20.note: The error text comes from the failure itself, so its exact wording varies.
steps: Send a question in a way that makes the answer fail, for example with the internet turned off before sending.
Look under the answer for the error text and a "Retry" button.
Turn the connection back on and click "Retry".
Check the failed answer is replaced by the new outcome for the same question.
S17.20.where: Side panel: when an answer fails, click the "Retry" button shown under the error text

S17.22.needs: a signed-in account, since the model list comes from the account
S17.22.note: The menu only appears when the account has managed model options; choosing a model also changes the chat's selected model, as the code applies it.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the "Try again" icon under the answer.
If a menu opens, check it has "Try again" and the heading "Try again with" followed by model names.
Choose a different model and check a new answer for the same question appears, and the model name under it is the one you chose.
S17.22.where: Side panel: on the latest answer, click the icon button labelled "Try again" to open the menu, then choose a model under "Try again with"

S17.36.note: Token counts and cost are not shown on the answer; only the model name and time. Expected asks for tokens and cost, which the code does not display.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Look in the action row under the answer for the model name followed by the time taken.
Hover the model name, if Auto picked the model, to see the tooltip "Auto chose this model: <reason>".
If the model was switched, look for the line "Moved to <model>: <reason>" above the action row.
S17.36.where: Side panel: under a finished answer, read the small line with the model name and the time; hover it for the auto-pick reason

S17.37.needs: a way to fail partway through an answer (for example losing the connection while text streams)
S17.37.note: The incomplete mark is the error text and Retry button; there is no separate word such as "Partial" in the code.
steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
While the text is still arriving, turn off the internet connection.
Check the text that already arrived stays on screen.
Check an error message appears under it with a "Retry" button, and that the answer is not shown as complete.
S17.37.where: Side panel: make an answer fail partway through, then look at the text already shown and the error footer under it

S17.39.note: The expected word is "stopped", but the visible word in the code is "Cancelled".
steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
While the text is still arriving, click the stop button, whose tooltip reads "Stop generating".
Check the text that arrived stays on screen.
Check the word "Cancelled" appears under it with a "Retry" button.
S17.39.where: Side panel: while an answer is still arriving, click the stop button labelled "Stop generating"

labels.text: No response was returned. Try again.

S17.40.needs: a way to get an empty reply, which is hard to force on purpose
S17.40.note: The code path is in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (empty-turn check); the tester may not be able to trigger it reliably.
steps: Send a message and wait for the turn to finish.
If the reply is empty, look for the text "No response was returned. Try again." with a "Retry" button in place of an empty bubble.
Click "Retry" and check a new attempt replaces the error.
S17.40.where: Side panel: a turn that finishes with no text shows "No response was returned. Try again." with a "Retry" button
